data.narrative:
Longshot Space is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Mike Grace and Nathan Saichek that has raised $10M+. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though no narrow peer set exists with sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints for direct median benchmarking.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using total raised ($10M) as a base proxy and applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields a $25M implied valuation. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure, which is standard for private companies. Peer-median methods failed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector—while 14 same-sector peers exist, only 5 public and 8 private companies were identified, with none meeting narrow filtering criteria.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered on $25M. This reflects conservative application of stage-based progression only. Key uncertainties include actual revenue run rate (which would enable P/S anchoring to public comps trading at 27.4x median), near-term funding momentum, and technical validation milestones. The methodology is constrained by data scarcity and reliance on a single method; broader conviction would require either revenue visibility or a denser comparable set at identical development stage.
